objective: Freeze the first source-faithful V15 menu-CSP cores after correcting the corrupted unpublished certificate. Classify degree-two path cores, degree-three rigid stars and the first rooted cycle pins without asserting C1 or root closure.

atomic_claims.text: The corrected V15 three-state menu has exactly thirty ordered legal length-two empty-middle paths; degree-two occurrences are locally recolorable.
With one third actual neighbor, exactly twenty-one leaf-unordered source-rigid stars remain, grouped into five complete neighbor-color families whose entire physical center list is menu-empty.
For the rooted four-state identity-pin cycle census, C4 has twenty-seven pinned source colorings and every one unpins by one nonroot recolor.

C5 has one hundred eighty rooted identity pins; exactly eighteen resist both one-vertex recoloring and uniform plus/minus-one shifts of nonroot subsets, while representative 13-0-7-15-4 has an explicit two-vertex repair to 13-0-7-14-1.

assumptions: Corrected V15 maps T8,T9,T10 and four-state menu I,T8,T9,T10.
All star incidences and every cycle closing edge are retained; a leaf is not treated as a permanent pin merely because its current color is frozen in one local table.
The clean finite certificate was independently regenerated inside the same generator trust domain after the previous certificate byte stream was found corrupted.
risks: No theorem shows a genuine C1 minimum obstruction contains one of the classified finite cores.
The C5 representative has a two-vertex repair and is not a root counterexample.
The companion all-size bridge-pruning proof remains an unverified candidate file in this same PR and is not promoted by the finite certificate.
No trusted verifier, Lean, SMT, EvidenceLink, Result or Solution admission occurred.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: The rooted C5 source coloring 13-0-7-15-4 resists every one-nonroot recolor and every uniform plus/minus-one nonroot-subset shift in the frozen four-state menu, but a two-vertex repair exists. Reject only those two local unpinning families.
